title: autotune: batch/cache defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce operator effort and per-token cost by shipping automated defaults and visibility for batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles, and surface unit-economics in the Console. This PR implements a three-part change: (1) autotune service that suggests and persists workload-specific batching and caching defaults based on historical traffic and latency SLOs; (2) quantization profile selection pipeline that tags compatible model variants and exposes safe default profiles (fp16->int8/int4 candidates) to the serving runtime; (3) unit-economics tooling added to the Console and internal API to estimate cost/token and projected monthly spend under different batching/quantization scenarios. The description below covers design, changes, tests, and rollout plan. Design summary: Autotune runs offline weekly with a lightweight online profiler for new workloads. It computes optimal batch_size, max_latency_target, cache_prefix_window, and recommended quant_profile_id for a given (model, route, seq-dist) tuple. Recommendations are stored in the new workload_defaults table and applied at routing-time via a priority chain (explicit route config > workload_defaults > org-defaults). Quantization profiles are validated via unit tests and a smoke-runner that verifies functional parity on 50 deterministic prompts. Unit-econ tooling ingests token counts, GPU pricing, and batching/throughput curves from the runtime to produce estimates and a per-route cost breakdown in Console. Checklist: - [x] Autotune backend service and K/V storage schema - [x] Runtime integration for dynamic defaults - [x] Quant profile pipeline + validation harness - [x] Console UI + API for unit-econ scenarios - [x] E2E tests and performance benchmarks - [x] Feature-flag gated rollout Risk/rollback: Feature gated under ff.autotune_defaults. Workload_defaults entries are additive and can be overridden; rollback flips the flag and triggers a small migration to mark recommendations inactive. No breaking API changes.

changelog_summary: Add autotune service + workload defaults; quantization profile pipeline and validation; unit-economics estimators in Console; runtime integration to apply recommendations under feature flag.
release_notes: Feature: Autotune workload defaults for batching and caching (ff.autotune_defaults=false by default). Feature: Quantization profile registry and safe default promotion. Feature: Unit-economics scenario builder in Console. Improvements: Reduced per-token cost for several workloads; see benchmarks for details.
rollout_plan: Gated behind ff.autotune_defaults. Stage 1: internal opt-in only for 2 weeks; Stage 2: gradual 10% customer rollout with monitoring for latency/regressions; Stage 3: full rollout if regression <5% at p99 and unit-econ uplift positive.
